clue.text: Media player screening very small crustacean

indicators.note: a screen hides something behind it, so the player's name is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: the iPod is Apple's portable media player
so can mean very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A gadget is used to show a film about a tiny shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice and their sea-dwelling relatives are tiny crustaceans of this order.

clue.text: Cook flaunting rice, fruitcakes around the edge?

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the following letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef shows off rice, alongside fruitcakes decorated round their rims.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'fruitcakes', slang for crazy people, sitting at the edge of a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremist members on the margins of a group are slangily called crazies at the movement's edge.

clue.text: European city not seldom seen, only every second!

indicators.note: taking only every second letter of the phrase skips the others in turn

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks that some city is seen often, though only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is a city in Europe.

clue.text: Time to taste role that's written up for The Quiet Man

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing a word upward means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to sip is to take a small taste
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor sampling a part written for the John Wayne film The Quiet Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns the whole string TSIPPART round. The Quiet Man is a 1952 film, but here it is a monk of an order known for keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of this Cistercian order are famed for their vow of silence, so one is a quiet man.

clue.text: Book of divination great without introduction, containing prominent feature

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
losing its introduction means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: big means great
the chin is a prominent feature of the face

explanation.surface: A fortune-telling book, great despite lacking a preface, with a striking feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without introduction' drops the first letter, and 'containing' wraps what is left round the facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Chinese classic is consulted to tell fortunes, a text for divining.

clue.text: Artistic genre with a lead singer?

definitions.meaning: a loud style of rock music, one genre of the arts
lead is a dense metal, so a singer made of lead would be one of these

explanation.surface: A style of art, complete with a frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: This rock style is a musical genre, and lead is a classic dense element of this kind.

clue.text: Put one's foot down on fraud, as one taken to court?

parts.note: to stamp on something is to squash it
a racket is a scam or fraudulent scheme

explanation.surface: Clamp down on a fraud, as befits someone being prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is not a law court but the walled court where the game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: This bat is carried onto the enclosed court where the indoor game is played.

clue.text: Man swigging last of lager tilted drink say, seeing retro food

indicators.note: a drinker swigging something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken
said aloud, the phrase gives a word of similar sound

parts.note: tilted is cocked, and a drink is ale, so the phrase is cocked ale

explanation.surface: A man knocking back lager from a tipped glass orders a nostalgic dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means COCKED ALE (tilted drink) is said aloud to give the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: This seafood starter in Marie Rose sauce is a 1970s classic, now seen as old-fashioned fare.

clue.text: Body part found in river — how distressing!

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
the arm is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A limb is discovered in a river, a grim find.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild exclamation expresses dismay, like 'oh dear'.

clue.text: 1/26th of the alphabet variety, we hear?

definitions.text: 1/26th of the alphabet variety, we hear?

parts.words: 1/26th of the alphabet variety, we hear?
parts.note: one letter of the alphabet is P, so a broth of only that letter would be 'P soup', which sounds like the dish

explanation.surface: A query about one letter's worth of alphabet soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Alphabet soup holds all twenty-six letters; one twenty-sixth of it is just the letter P, pronounced like the green vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick broth of green legumes sounds just like soup of the letter P.

clue.text: Antonym poetic?

definitions.meaning: written in poetry rather than prose, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: An opposite is the reverse of something; split, the word means written as poetry.

clue.text: Skill of the under-twos football team?

definitions.text: Skill of the under-twos football team?

parts.words: Skill of the under-twos football team?
parts.note: running with the ball at your feet is a football skill, and babies under two famously let saliva run from their mouths

explanation.surface: A question about what toddlers excel at on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Running the ball close to the feet is a football skill; drooling is what infants do.

clue.text: Daft issue — potential trouble

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy or daft
issue means offspring, one's kin

explanation.surface: A silly matter that could cause problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery peel is the cartoon cause of a fall, so it means a likely pitfall.

clue.text: Cutter, someone a grand in debt?

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, and a grand is a thousand pounds
someone in debt owes, and one who owes is an ower

explanation.surface: A question whether some cutter is a person owing a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn machine cuts grass, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: The certified tale in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: An authenticated story appears in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book the tale is in, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the word 'the' is the English determiner of this type.

clue.text: Wood outstanding conductor ultimately under Diaghilev, totally gutted for composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another comes after it
a gutted word loses all its insides, leaving only its outer letters
read as out-standing, one piece stands outside the other

parts.note: oak is a wood

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Henry Wood, a fine conductor, ended up under the ballet impresario Diaghilev, who was thoroughly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' makes ORAK; 'totally gutted' strips Diaghilev to its two ends. Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms, and 'Wood' is the tree here.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin, the Czech author of the New World Symphony, wrote music.

clue.text: Dead stupid miners stealing diamonds — something more to say?

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so its letters are muddled too
a thief stealing takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Foolish miners taking gems, a story with a postscript to come?
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix adds material to a text, an extra thing to say.

clue.text: Bulb lit, one lit

parts.note: a light that is lit is on
I is the Roman numeral one
again, lit means switched on

explanation.surface: One light bulb is lit, and another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a lamp, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable grows as a layered underground bulb.

clue.text: I shop for food etc madly after five, that is to say

indicators.note: the rest of the pieces come after the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
a deli is a shop selling food

indicators.note: acting madly means wildly, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shopper visits a deli for groceries and so on in a frenzy after five o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin term, abbreviated viz, means namely.

clue.text: Treatment provided by way of elderly relative getting end away?

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a grandad given a remedy so he can still have sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it drops the N of GRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This erectile dysfunction drug is a medical treatment.

clue.text: Bouncer in row, confiscating goods

indicators.note: confiscating something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
G stands for good, so two of them are goods

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman in a dispute takes away some merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman, but it is the tiger who bounces in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's tiger character is famous for constant bouncing.

clue.text: One of twelve, a US city

parts.note: August is one of the twelve months of the year

explanation.surface: A US city that is one of a dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Maine and a Georgia city famed for golf both bear this name.

clue.text: One identifying opener being sent back

indicators.note: sending something back returns it, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a gateman opens the gate

explanation.surface: A doorman being returned to where he came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge with your name on it serves to identify you.

clue.text: Titan, perhaps, down one's pants

definitions.meaning: Titan is the largest satellite of Saturn, one example
to bare one's buttocks with trousers dropped, as a prank

explanation.surface: A giant of myth drops his trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is a satellite of Saturn; baring one's backside is slang for the same word as a verb.

clue.text: Tower of strength in Sun editor I gathered — that should make you laugh!

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
gathered together means collected in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ox tows heavy loads and is proverbially strong

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper editor hails a pillar of support, a cheerful note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower of strength' is an idiom for a supporter, but here a tower is something that tows. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gas is the dentist's anaesthetic named for making patients giggle.
